ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in the figure, an electron (with mass $m$) and charge $e$ enters a uniform electric field with an initial velocity $v_{0}$ along the direction of the electric field lines. The magnitude of the uniform electric field is $E$, and gravity is negligible. The question is:

1. What is the acceleration of an electron moving in an electric field?
2. What is the maximum distance an electron can travel into an electric field?
3. What is the kinetic energy when the electron reaches half of the maximum distance in the electric field?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, an electron (with mass $m$) and charge $e$ enters a uniform electric field with an initial velocity $v_{0}$ along the direction of the electric field lines. The magnitude of the uniform electric field is $E$, and gravity is negligible. The question is: 1. What is the acceleration of an electron moving in an electric field? 2. What is the maximum distance an electron can travel into an electric field? 3. What is the kinetic energy when the electron reaches half of the maximum distance in the electric field?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows several parallel horizontal electric-field lines with arrowheads pointing to the right, labeled E. The electron is drawn with a minus sign, and its initial velocity arrow v0 also points to the right, the same direction as the field lines. Reasoning: Because the particle is an electron, its charge is negative; if e denotes the magnitude of the electron charge, then q=-e. Taking the positive x-axis to the right, the electric force is F=qE=-eE, so the acceleration is a=F/m=-eE/m, i.e. leftward with magnitude eE/m. For the maximum distance into the field, the electron slows until v=0. Using v^2=v0^2+2ax with a=-eE/m gives 0=v0^2-2(eE/m)x_max, so x_max=mv0^2/(2eE). At half this distance, x=x_max/2. Then v^2=v0^2-2(eE/m)(x_max/2)=v0^2-(eE/m)x_max=v0^2-v0^2/2=v0^2/2. Therefore the kinetic energy is K=(1/2)m(v0^2/2)=mv0^2/4.
